$comment: Hand-written content carried into the generated prop pages, the counterpart of _style-page-content.json. Keyed by kind id (the AnyProp definition name minus 'Prop', lowercased), with `sections` rendered after the generated sections in declared order. Everything derivable from component.schema.json or the binding files lives THERE; this file holds only the judgment calls and narratives no schema member states. Extracted from site/src/content/docs/schema/props.md when the generated tree replaced it.

sections.States: A boolean prop named by a [`specs.states`](/schema/conventions/#specs-members) entry is a state concept, not an ordinary parameter. Whether it stays in the emitted contract follows the concept's disposition — browser-managed concepts (hover, focus, active) leave the contract entirely, consumer-set ones (disabled, selected, invalid) stay and also surface as an aria attribute. The rule's case table is the [statesToContract](/schema/mappings/react/clusters/states-to-contract/) cluster, shared by both emitters and the CSS transform.

string.intro: A `StringProp` is distinguished from an `EnumProp` by the absence of `enum` — the two share `type: string`, and the closed list is what separates a value set the library enumerates from one it leaves open.

enum.intro: A prop of `type: string` without an `enum` is a [`StringProp`](/schema/props/string/).

sections.States: An enum prop named by a [`specs.states`](/schema/conventions/#specs-members) entry participates in state classification exactly as a boolean does — see the [statesToContract](/schema/mappings/react/clusters/states-to-contract/) cluster. An enum whose entries are all state values can leave the emitted contract entirely when every concept naming it is browser-managed.

sections.Constraints: Slot constraint members (`minChildren`, `maxChildren`, `anyOf`) are emitted when [`conventions.platforms.figma.slotConstraints`](/schema/conventions/#platform-members) is declared.

sections.Where an authoring default lives:
An authoring-default image sits in one of two places, and they describe different things:

| Location | Describes |
|----------|-----------|
| [`ImageBinding.examples`](/schema/prop-configurations/) | The image at *that binding site* — how one consumer placed it |
| `ImageProp.examples` | The image *the component itself* was authored with |

Where both apply to one rendered instance, the binding is the more specific statement. A designated image component is the origin of an image rather than a consumer of one, so it has no binding site in its own spec — `examples` on the prop is its only home for this.

`examples` is non-contractual reference material, parallel to `StringProp.examples`, and is distinct from `default`: a default states what the prop resolves to when a consumer omits it, while examples only demonstrate typical content.

```yaml
props:
  imageSource:
    type: image
    examples:
      - $image: "#/components/dsImage/images/dsImage__image"
```

sections.Figma folding:
```yaml
props:
  margin:
    type: object
    members:
      compact:
        type: string
        default: none
        enum: [none, small, large]
      expanded:
        type: string
        default: none
        enum: [none, small, large]
```

Figma authors members as separator-delimited flat property names (`margin.compact`, `margin.expanded`), folded into one `ObjectProp` when [`conventions.platforms.figma.objectProps`](/schema/conventions/#platform-members) is declared. Each member's `$extensions['com.figma'].name` records the flat source name, so unfolding back to Figma is reversal, not re-derivation. Configurations set an object prop with a member-keyed value — see [Prop Configurations](/schema/prop-configurations/).

sections.Primitive content markers:
`anyOf` is the one list of what a slot accepts. Alongside component names it carries reserved markers naming a **primitive** kind:

| Marker | Admits |
|--------|--------|
| `$text` | A text primitive — a plain string fill |
| `$glyph` | A glyph primitive — an icon fill |

```yaml
props:
  children:
    type: slot
    defaultSlot: true
    anyOf: [$glyph, $text, badge]   # a glyph, a label, or a composed Badge
  description:
    type: slot
    anyOf: [$text, link]            # accepts a primitive, and is not the default slot
```

`anyOf: [$text]` is a text-only slot — no component permitted. `anyOf: [badge]` is Badge-only — no primitive permitted. Absent means any component and no primitive, which is what every slot without markers means today.

The names are the ones [`anatomy`](/schema/anatomy/) items already use, so `type: text` on an element and `$text` here are the same primitive. The `$` prefix marks a value the contract reserves rather than one the library supplies — the same role it plays in `$token`, `$binding` and `$slotContent`, extended from keys to values. A component key can never shadow a marker, because the safe key grammar admits no leading `$`.

A marker is recorded when the slot's default content in Figma held a top-level primitive of that kind, in at least one variant, and [`slotPrimitives`](/settings/slot-primitives/) is on — which it is unless the library turns it off. A marker only ever joins an `anyOf` that already names at least one component; a slot whose detected content is primitives alone carries no `anyOf`, because `anyOf` is a constraint and `[$text]` would say only a text primitive may fill the slot. Those primitives are not emitted as anatomy elements — the slot is — and their formatting travels on the slot element's [`contentStyles`](/schema/elements/#styles-vs-content-styles), keyed by the same markers.

Markers and `defaultSlot` are orthogonal. A Button's `children` accepts primitives *and* is the default slot; an Alert's `description` accepts a primitive and is *not* the default; a layout component's slots are default-eligible and take components only.

sections.The default slot:
`defaultSlot` marks the one slot a layout component always composes through. It is set at generation time, when the prop's name matched the library's [`specs.slots.default.match`](/schema/conventions/#slots) convention, and is read off the spec thereafter — a consumer needs no access to those conventions to know which slot it is.

An instance filling a `defaultSlot` prop may be nested as a plain [child](/schema/children/) rather than through a [`SlotContentRef`](/schema/slot-content-ref/). Every other slot binds explicitly, which is the only shape that can say *which* of several slots a fill belongs to.

**At most one `SlotProp` per component may be `true`.** This is a constraint over sibling entries in one `props` map, which JSON Schema cannot express without reaching into a named prop's value to compare it against its siblings. It is therefore an authoring and generator contract, not schema-validated: `specs generate` marks at most one and reports a component whose declared convention matches several, and a hand-authored spec that breaks the invariant is malformed input a consumer may reject.

extensionsPage.intro: The `$extensions` object on a prop definition holds vendor-specific metadata under reverse-domain keys. Currently only the `com.figma` extension is defined. Extension data is provenance — a consumer MUST NOT need it to interpret the prop (the spec contract carries everything semantic), and the render direction reads it to reverse what capture recorded.

sections.Scenarios:
Every shape below is one `specs generate` actually writes, keyed by what produced it. A prop may combine them — `name` joins whatever else the prop's extraction recorded.

**A two-option VARIANT read as a boolean.** The axis's options were exactly true/false, so the prop is a `BooleanProp`; the recorded type is what tells render to rebuild a variant axis rather than a BOOLEAN property.

```yaml
isCompact:
  type: boolean
  default: false
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      type: VARIANT
```

**A consolidated visibility pair.** A BOOLEAN property only ever toggled the element this content prop fills, so the boolean was consumed into the content prop's nullability and named here — render re-creates it.

```yaml
badgeLabel:
  type: string
  nullable: true
  default: null
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      visibilityProp: showBadge
```

**A code-only prop from a hidden TEXT layer.** String- or number-valued; `source` names the sub-layer so render can mint the hidden layer back.

```yaml
headingLevel:
  type: number
  default: 2
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      type: TEXT
      source:
        kind: codeOnlyProp
        layer: headingLevel
```

**A code-only enum from a nested instance.** The nested component's variant options define the enum values, and `instanceOf` names which component — a two-option true/false instance mints a boolean through the same shape.

```yaml
role:
  type: string
  default: status
  enum: [status, alert, log]
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      type: VARIANT
      source:
        kind: codeOnlyProp
        layer: role
        instanceOf: RoleOptions
```

**A code-only image prop.** Minimal by design (ADR-063): the authoring-default image rides on the `ImageBinding` at the binding site, not here.

```yaml
imageSource:
  type: image
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      type: TEXT
      source:
        kind: codeOnlyProp
        layer: imageSource
```

**A key the formatting could not reconstruct (ADR-066).** The Figma property name fell outside the safe key grammar — or was already in the destination format — so `name` records it and reversal is a lookup, not a re-derivation.

```yaml
showIcon:
  type: boolean
  default: true
  $extensions:
    com.figma:
      name: "Show icon?"
```

**A folded object-prop member (ADR-111).** Each member records the separator-delimited flat property name it folded from; the parent `ObjectProp` records nothing — it has no Figma counterpart of its own.

```yaml
margin:
  type: object
  members:
    compact:
      type: string
      default: none
      enum: [none, small, large]
      $extensions:
        com.figma:
          name: margin.compact
```
